column5: The chatbot based natural-language query tool is innovative. My main question is whether it can be made reliable enough for real-world usage.
column7: Getting the chat assisted SQL queries to be reliable is going to be a potentially very difficult task.
column9: Would like to see more thought put on what type of person might use this--what's their job, what are they trying to do, etc.

column5: Use of OpenRouter for LLM is novel. The use of the natural language chat is also pretty novel in comparison with other teams.
column7: Appreciate the research they did into the existing archeticture (e.g., AWS) and use that to develop there.  The work they did to check the accuracy of NestChat is appreciated. An additional feature to have experts and non-experts develop bounding boxes would be good to see built out.
column9: Many of the future directions could have a big impact on future work In particular the potential for classification route.
column10: NestScope includes NestChat and NestVision. NestChat uses SQL queries. Nest Vision is a finetuned YOLO model. Appreciate the presentation of the system architecture. The presentation itself could have been a bit more organized. I recommend polishing for the final presentation if you move on to the next rond. Also, double check you data.

column5: The text-to-SQL chatbot for conservation data access was very creative. Making complex datasets usable for non-technical users is a real strength.
column7: The system design and performance were impressive.
column9: Lowering barriers to data access could dramatically speed up research and restoration planning. This has strong practical value.
column10: The accessibility focus with the natural language queries really stood out.
